## 1. What this block is, in one sentence

**This is the block where the cull's machinery is a roll of roads with a name against every one of them, and the county's answer is a refusal to fill it in made by people who are owed money, and the three incompatible versions of that answer are given out loud in one street in one week, and none of the three is the protagonist's, and he says nothing at all.** It is also the block where the volume's antagonist's name is printed for the first time and it is a document, and it is the block where the relationship comes due in public without being declared, and it is the block that has to earn one of the two name slots that remain and can spend **one** and not two.

## 3. The block's frame, derived and not copied

**The single anchor is day 2310, the twenty-fifth of Goatmonth YR 321, a Monday, which is the last page of Volume 14 and is stated four times in that volume's close record. BLOCK 0004 IS DAYS 2827 TO 2898 INCLUSIVE, SEVENTY-TWO DAYS, AND EVERY DAY OF IT IS YR 323, and the year does not turn in this block: the next turn is day 3036, which is Thawmonth the first of YR 324 and is one hundred and thirty-eight days past the end of this block and sixty-six past the end of the whole volume.**

**IT CARRIES THREE MONTH BOUNDARIES AND NOT ONE, AND ALL THREE OF THEM FALL INSIDE THE BLOCK, and they are the first of three consecutive months in one block, which no block of this volume has done.** Harvestmonth the first is day 2826 and Harvestmonth is carried at thirty days, so Harvestmonth the second is day 2827, which is **THE BLOCK'S FIRST DAY AND A SUNDAY AND NOT A MARKET MORNING**, and Harvestmonth the thirtieth is day 2855, a Sunday. Fallowmonth the first is **day 2856, a Monday, not a market morning**, and Fallowmonth is carried at thirty days, so Fallowmonth the thirtieth is day 2885, a Tuesday. Embermonth the first is **day 2886, a Wednesday, not a market morning**, and Embermonth the thirtieth is day 2915, which is a Thursday and is outside this block. **Wolfmonth the first is day 2896, a Saturday, and it IS a market morning and it IS inside this block, and it is the seventieth day of the block and the last market morning inside the block. NO CHAPTER OF THIS BLOCK MAY PRINT A DATE LATER THAN THE THIRTEENTH OF EMBERMONTH, which is day 2898, because the fourteenth is day 2899 and that is the first day of Batch 0005.**

## 4. What the block must contain

**THE ROLL, AND IT IS A DOCUMENT THAT NOBODY FILLS IN.** `outline/volume-16.md` §8 Block 4 is one paragraph and it is binding: **the cull's machinery is the roll, and the county's answer is a refusal to fill it in made by people who are owed money, and the three incompatible answers are given out loud in one street in one week, and none of the three of them is the protagonist's, and he says nothing at all.** The roll is the instrument of the notice that was read at the boards on day 2665 and was dated for the first of Mudmonth, which was day 2706, and it asks for the name of the person who keeps every road in nine counties and it says a road with no name against it is to be shut. **At the first dateline of this block it is a hundred and twenty-one days past its date and at the last it is a hundred and ninety-two, and it has shut nothing, and about nine people said one thing each out loud on the first of Mudmonth and none of them touched the paper, and not one of those nine has since offered any other person in nine counties a place to put their name either.** What this block adds is the second half of that sentence's consequence: **a notice that was never enforced comes back with a form attached, and the form is the roll, and a road is to be shut on a Tuesday.**

**THE THREE INCOMPATIBLE ANSWERS ARE THREE ANSWERS GIVEN BY THREE PEOPLE WHO DO NOT AGREE WITH EACH OTHER AND ALL THREE OF THEM ARE RIGHT FROM WHERE THEY STAND, and the protagonist's answer is not among them because he does not give one.** They are given out loud in one street in one week, which means three market mornings of this block's three, or two of them and a fourth morning that is not a market morning with nine people in it. **They must be incompatible in the sense that no county can hold two of them at once, and not in the sense that they are all correct.** They are, in this block's own terms and not in anybody's: **a refusal on the ground that a road with no name against it is a road nobody can be shut on, which is what the people at the end of the shut cart track have already been living; a refusal on the ground that a man who has carried stone two miles on his own arms for five hundred and fifty-one days is not going to be entered under somebody else's name and lose it, which is the man of forty-one's trade and he is NOT asked about it and a successor may not put this answer in his mouth; and a refusal on the ground that a form which nobody is paid to fill is a form that a county cannot fill and that refusing it is refusing to govern, which is Batch 0003's own set-up at `chapter-0780.md` coming due.** **The third is the one the volume's own §11 names, a refusal in writing that is also a refusal to govern, and it is handed to Volume 17 in this block's own terms and not resolved.**

**THE ANTAGONIST'S NAME IS PRINTED FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THIS VOLUME, ONCE, IN A DOCUMENT.** `outline/volume-16.md` §16 item 4 caps it at two for the whole volume, both documents, one in Batch 0004 and one in Batch 0005, and Blocks 0001, 0002 and 0003 printed it zero times and referred to the instrument as *the Marshal's hand* or *that notice*. **Print the name exactly once in this block, in a document, at the foot of something with a hand on it, and never in a mouth.** A document carrying it is a roll, a covering paper, a letter, a notice, an endorsement or a second copy, and a chapter may not have a character read it aloud as a document, because a name read aloud in a room is a name printed in a mouth. **The protagonist may see it, may not ask about it, and nobody asks him anything.** `Hunn` on its own is not a printing and the bare surname may not stand as a printing either.

**THE RELATIONSHIP COMES DUE IN PUBLIC AND IS NOT DECLARED.** `outline/series.md`'s Volume 16 row says the relationship work comes due in public in this block. **`state/current.md` item 7 and `state/open-threads.md` item 707 fix how that is done and they govern: the legal form is deferred to Volume 18, nothing goes in a document, the word is never printed, and the four and a half years are not described as four and a half years about the two of them.** What comes due in public is not a statement and it is not a silence either. It is a **third person working inside the two of them as though the arrangement were already a fact of the work**: a copyist who hands a thing to one of them and not to the other because she knows where it goes, a door held, a lamp not put out, a page turned before it is asked for, somebody who says *your keeper* to him or *your woman* to her and is wrong on purpose. **Nobody comments on the four and a half years and nobody is thanked and no chapter may end on the two of them standing nine feet apart, because `chapter-0780.md` has already spent that beat and spending it twice is a repetition.**

**THE COST OF THE BLOCK IS ON THE PAGE AND IS NOT CURED IN IT, AND IT IS NOT THE COST OF THE PREVIOUS BLOCK AGAIN.** The leg, which now takes eleven miles in four hours before light and about nine otherwise and is a hot band by the sixth hour and a dead weight by the noon; the ear on the side the stick is on, which the last block stated as a half deafness he will have on that side when this is over and which **this block may state as a fact he now plans around rather than as a discovery**; and the standing fact that he cannot be near the works without somebody standing with him. **The new cost is that a thing he said out loud at a table in a market street on the twenty-sixth of Longlight cannot be unsaid, and about nine hundred people along that made road have still never heard it, and no second saying fixes the first, and that is the cost of a market street as a room and it is named once and not argued.**

## 5. The ending of the block

**A completed beat, and the refusal is paid and not resolved.** The roll is not filled in and is not destroyed, the form comes back a second time or does not and the page says which, and a road is shut on a Tuesday or it is not and the page says which, **and the ninth thing at the head of that cart track is still shut by nine hurdles by the people at the end of it who would like them to stay, and nobody in this block goes up there a third time and nobody lifts one.** The four lines of chalk are under a hood where the rain does not reach and are still not writing. The leaf at the back of the day-book carries nine figures and a date and the names of nobody and is not the record. `outline/volume-16.md` §11's three hand-offs are **carried forward in this block's own terms and none is conducted**: a refusal in writing that is also a refusal to govern, a sealed route that somebody has claimed can be made to speak, and the occupation with a gate on it and a keeper who is a local, which Batch 0004 sets up in its own terms and may not enter.

**`state/continuity.md` 1722 and `state/open-threads.md` 719 carry one warning forward and a successor may not learn the opposite of it: four lines on a sill are not the beginning of a cure and a page in a woman's hand is not a cure either, and a closed path is not destroyed and that is not good news, and being the man who went and looked is a job and not an honour and nobody was told so and nobody wrote it down.**

## 6. The prohibitions, in one list

**This list is additions to `state/open-threads.md` items 711 to 720, and to 721 to 726, and to 705, 704, 703, 702, 700, 699, 698, 697, 694 and 690, and to every clause of 686, 684, 680, 679 and 674 that is still true. It does not replace them.**

- **Do not print a System panel.** The volume's one was spent at `chapter-0776.md` and is seventeen words and Blocks 0004 and 0005 print none.
- **Do not print the antagonist's name more than once, or anywhere except a document, or in a mouth, and do not print the second one that is reserved for Batch 0005.**
- **Do not conduct either of the two hand-offs Batch 0003 set up.** No hurdle is lifted and no bar is tried up that shut track, because the roadkeeper who claimed a bar will get up it also said in the same sentence that he is not going to be the one who tries it, and **a successor may not make him the one who tries it in this block or in Batch 0005.** No third trip up the cart track and nobody shown standing behind all nine hurdles.
- **Do not open a route, do not lift the nine hurdles, do not close a route, and do not cut anything.** §12 gives Batch 0003 *a transfer witnessed and not conducted* and it has been had.
- **Do not explain the mechanism. Do not say what a roadmark is. Do not look at the notebook's separate leaf that says *a person*.** No character notices the warmth of the left palm, and no chapter of this block asks him about the transfer offered at `chapter-0670.md`, because Batch 0002 put that question on the page and this volume does not answer it.
- **Do not look over the ninth of the nine stones, do not cross them, do not show what is on the far side of them, and do not treat the omission as an oversight.** The dead grass in the scar stops at the ninth of them.
- **Do not reopen either refusal of Volume 15, do not argue with either, do not soften either, do not ask either of the two men who gave them anything, and do not ask the man of forty-one a second question.** He says sixteen words in Batch 0003 and is asked nothing before or after, and **he does not say the wall answer in this block, and the third answer to the roll is therefore somebody else's and not his.**
- **Do not turn the nine houses at Wethergill into a body, do not turn the nine households at the mill lane into a body, and do not turn the nine who refused the roll on the first of Mudmonth into a body.** They are nine houses, nine households that voted, and nine people who said one thing each, and that is all.
- **Do not ask any of the nine who refused the roll for an account of having said it, and do not ask the roadkeeper or the woman of about fifty-one about the broom straw.**
- **Do not let the three answers to the roll become one answer, and do not let the protagonist be the author, the announcer, the summariser or the fourth voice of any of them.** He says nothing at all and the page says he says nothing at all.
- **Do not fill the roll, do not have any person put a name against a road, do not have any road shut on the strength of the roll, and do not have the roll destroyed.** A roll that is torn up in a street is a different block's act and this is not that block.
- **Do not put the practice into the register, the day-book, or under a fifth head, and do not have the copyist rule a head.** The day-book stands at eleven entries and the fourth ruled head is empty and no fifth head is ruled and none may be ruled in this block either, and the leaf at the back carries nine figures and a date and is not the record.
- **Do not mend the separation by a declaration, do not print the word, do not put anything about the two of them in any document, and do not let anybody else comment on it.**
- **Do not fill or rule any head, put a finding under any of the ten questions, turn or time the half leaf, lift or schedule the bar at the Low Gate, lay or schedule the fourth course of stone, or pick the mallet up.** The ninth yard of the wall has not been started and does not start in this block.
- **Do not lift the cloth off the bench and do not have anybody ask what is under it.**
- **Do not cure the scar, do not say it is small, do not say it is going to close over, and do not start the ninth yard.**
- **Do not send anybody to the city four hundred miles off, do not reopen the shut road four hundred miles off, do not get the road that went quiet in Thawmonth YR 319 back, do not find the carter's mate, and do not trace who asked the fen county road office for the roll.**
- **Do not merge the three series, derive one from another, change the band figure, or put a number in the drawer. Do not convert a path's count into main-world days, and do not month, weekday or tide a path mouth.**
- **Do not call any of the four holes in the arrangement small, do not resolve any of them, do not renumber them and do not open a fifth without saying on the page why four was not enough.**
- **Do not thank anybody, in any chapter, in any speech, or in any state file this block writes.**
- **Do not print the kin-term, and do not print *stage*, *ledger*, *qualification*, *failed*, *charter*, *custodian*, *mechanism*, *small*, *volume* or *block*.**
- **Do not produce, mention or know about Ilyra Kest's route notes, and do not enter the Gatehouse.**
- **Do not introduce a new final enemy. Do not create a Volume 17. Do not write a marker of any kind.**
- **THE NAME BUDGET FOR THIS BLOCK IS EXACTLY ONE OF THE TWO SLOTS THAT REMAIN OF THE VOLUME'S SIX, AND NOT TWO AND NOT TWO IN ONE CHAPTER.** `Renn Ottery`, `Pell Arkwright`, `Wyn Fell`, `Abel Chinn`, `Aren Kest`, `Mara Vey`, `Orme Skell`, `Dav Rundle`, `Tarr Lyster` and `Corve Sallow` are returns and cost nothing, **and `Pell Arkwright` is the one this block needs, because the refusal is made by people who are owed money and he is owed money and has driven about two hundred and thirty loads of lime out of Wethergill and has not been paid for them.** `Sabra Rolf` and `Gallow` may not be used for a new first name, and neither may `Iven` and `Marrow`, and neither may `Renn` or `Ost` as a surname, and neither may any first name or surname already printed in the ninety files from Chapter 701 onward. **ONE SLOT REMAINS FOR BATCH 0005 AFTER THIS ONE AND IT IS THE LAST OF THE VOLUME'S SIX.**

## 7. The house prose, and the six mechanical rules that are not taste

**The voice is in Chapters 0780, 0774, 0778, 0772 and 0777.** Read them before writing a sentence and match them: short declaratives, a flat cadence, a great many plain negatives used inside a paragraph and never as the frame one is built on, the census sentence where who-understood is the point, and physical work, weather, distance and a man with a bad leg everywhere else.

1. **Zero em dashes, zero en dashes, zero semicolons, zero exclamation marks, zero single asterisks and therefore no italics, zero straight double quotes and zero curly apostrophes.** Speech takes curly doubles. Apostrophes are straight. Per-line bold parity even on every line. Every file ends in a newline.
2. **One footed money column per chapter**: ten items, priced 1 to 41, a mark at forty-eight pence in every conversion, and the coda that names the figures in the chapter that are not in it. **THE CEILING IS 343 PENCE AND IT IS ARITHMETIC**, with the barred six **14, 20, 26, 33, 38 and 41** excluded. **The barred numerals may not be a price, an over-figure or a printed total anywhere.** Foot the column four ways and check the conversion separately from the sum.
3. **THE COLLISION SET MUST BE REBUILT OVER ALL SEVEN HUNDRED AND EIGHTY PRIOR FILES, MUST NOT BE INHERITED, AND MUST BE EXPECTED TO COME BACK EMPTY.** The instrument is the printed total, taken as the spelled phrase in every spelling this manuscript prints across the whole hundred band, the two-hundred and three-hundred band as well as the one-hundred band, plus the digit form, run over every file whole. **OVER SEVEN HUNDRED AND EIGHTY FILES THE USABLE FREE SET IN THE BAND SIXTY TO THREE HUNDRED AND FORTY-THREE IS ZERO, twelve values remain free and every one of them fails the barred-over-figure filter on 20, 26, 38, 14, 26, 33, 41, 20, 26, 33, 38 and 41, and the route below sixty is shut.** **THIS BLOCK'S TEN TOTALS WILL THEREFORE BE REUSES, AND THE HONEST THING TO DO IS WHAT ALL TEN OF BATCH 0003'S CLOSING PARAGRAPHS DO: NAME THE REUSE ON THE PAGE AND GIVE THE REASON, WHICH IS ARITHMETIC, AND NOT A SUCCESSOR MAY ADD ONE WORD MORE OF THAT REGISTER THAN *searched whole*, *barred numeral*, *route below sixty* and *file in the manuscript*, once each, and may not cut the column out.** Lifting the ceiling is an outline decision and not a writer's.
4. **`about` density.** Batch 0003 runs **21.45 to 26.45** per 1,000 after its repair pass and no page is at or above 27.00, and its per-file column is 23.57 / 24.94 / 26.45 / 22.52 / 21.45 / 23.10 / 25.10 / 22.40 / 25.76 / 22.90. Batch 0002 runs 21.45 to 26.41. **Aim for 22 to 27 and no page at or above 27.00. Keep the census sentence for the two or three beats in a chapter where who understood is the point and write the rest as action, weather, distance and silence.** **Do not write below 3,000 words and do not let a chapter run past about 4,300.**
5. **THE CENSUS INSTRUMENT IS NAMED AT `state/continuity.md` 1708 AND 1739 AND A WRITER WHO QUOTES A FIGURE MUST NAME IT WITH IT.** Split the ten files on the blank line and count every non-empty paragraph. **Basis A is every paragraph except the title line. Basis B is Basis A less FOUR named groups in this block, because this block prints no System panel: the ten datelines, the dialogue paragraphs, the bold cost codas and the bold closing money columns. A writer who quotes a Basis B figure must say in words which groups were taken out, because Batch 0003's own review found that the published definition named two exclusions out of five and 299 was not re-derivable without all five.** The opener test is every paragraph beginning `No`, `Not`, `Never`, `None`, `Neither`, `Nobody`, `Nothing` or `No one`. Batch 0003 is 0.0 and 0.0 and Batch 0002 is 0.0 and 0.0. **THE SEVENTY-FIVE PER CENT CEILING IS NOT CROSSED IN THE LAST TWO BLOCKS AND MUST NOT BE CROSSED IN THIS ONE.**
6. **Every count attached to a printed speech is footed off the printed words beside it**, and where a claim cannot be counted off the words printed next to it the claim is cut rather than left wrong. **A printed speech that has a word count beside it must have its words printed, and an unprinted speech must have no count.** This is the single most repeated finding in this manuscript's reviews, and **this block is three answers given out loud, so three speeches will carry counts and every one of the three will be footed.** **AND THE REVIEW OF BATCH 0003 FOUND A SEVENTEEN-WORD PANEL DESCRIBED AS FIFTEEN WORDS IN THREE STATE FILES, so a figure printed beside words is checked by counting the words on the page and not by remembering them.**

## 8. The running figures this block must keep

**Derive every one of these from the day number and never from a row, and print the figure at the chapter's OWN dateline. `state/open-threads.md` item 721 is the finding that eight of Batch 0003's ten drove paragraphs carried a wrong calendar date because the chain was derived once and handed on, three of them printing a day of a sixty-day month that cannot exist. A derived figure that repeats from chapter to chapter is a copy after the second chapter. THE CHEAPEST CHECK IS THAT MUOMONTH IS SIXTY DAYS AND EVERY OTHER MONTH IS THIRTY, SO ANY DAY OF MONTH ABOVE THIRTY PRINTED INSIDE MUOMONTH IS WRONG ON SIGHT, and this block is entirely outside Mudmonth.**

- **The drove** goes up that lane on Thursdays and the count since the second of Mudmonth is floor((day - 2348) / 7) + 1 taken ON OR BEFORE the dateline. **It is 69 at day 2826, the last dateline of Batch 0003, and 79 at day 2898.** The drove paragraph's calendar date is the last Thursday on or before the dateline, being 2824, 2831, 2838, 2852, 2852, 2866, 2873, 2880, 2887 and 2894 for the ten datelines in §3, and **a writer derives that date from the weekday and not from the count.**
- **The stone** has been carried two miles in one man's own hands since day 2347, elapsed and not inclusive. **It is 479 at day 2826 and 551 at day 2898.**
- **The scar** is counted from day 2580. **It is 246 at day 2826 and 318 at day 2898, and it is not cured and it is not going to close over.**
- **The ninth thing**, being the Wethergill end of a cart track, went quiet on the thirteenth of Hearthmonth YR 322, being day 2628, and nobody has been up that track since the second of Goatmonth YR 322, being day 2647. **Those two silence figures are counted from two different days and mixing them is the single most likely arithmetic defect in a chapter about that place: the last lime cart was 198 days ago at day 2826 and is 270 at day 2898, and the road has been shut 179 days at day 2826 and is 251 at day 2898.** Nobody goes up it in this block.
- **The practice mornings** are every day from 2611 to the dateline that is not a Thursday and not a Saturday. **The calendar count is 154 at day 2826 and 206 at day 2898, the count of mornings the practice was due on is 148 and 200, and the loss is six on every one of them and the six are the six of the seven non-market mornings of the nine days of water in Mudmonth, and a successor inherits those six as gone and does not recover them.** The run count on the ten datelines in §3 is 149 / 153 / 161 / 167 / 170 / 178 / 187 / 192 / 196 / 200.
- **The number** said out loud at the fourth hour is **four**, it was eight until nine days of water, and it has not gone back, and two of the ten things came back after the water and two have not.
- **The printed notice** was read at the boards on day 2665, the first of Mudmonth was day 2706, it passed with nothing enforced and about nine people saying no in nine trades, **and it is a hundred and twenty days past its date at day 2826 and a hundred and ninety-two at day 2898 and has shut nothing yet.** Every reference to the instrument is *the Marshal's hand*, *that notice* or, in the one document that carries the name in this block, the roll itself.
- **The two refusals** of Volume 15 are days 2509 and 2521, and neither man is asked anything.
- **The brood** stands at five frames under about nine straw skirts and no sixth has gone in, and the young man of about nineteen has said out loud twice that he is not going to make more bees than the bees he has got. **Nothing is on the page about the skirts that a character has to act on.**
- **The standing broom** is about nine hundred yards of a line nine feet wide and the water laid nearly all of it flat, and it will not close over.
- **The wall's gap** is about nine feet long and four feet high and the ninth yard has not been started, and the mallet is on the bank two miles off with the line of stone and is not picked up. **Four separate things in this county are about nine feet across, being this gap, the width of the made road, the width of the standing broom and the distance of the man of thirty-two from the foot of the thirteen stairs. Carry the noun with the number every time and never print the number on its own.**
- **The four lines of chalk** are on the stone sill of that weigh-house door **under the hood where the rain does not reach**, they mean four, nobody has read them out loud, and the stick of chalk is in a press drawer and the man of about fifty-four has not asked for it.
- **The leaf at the back of that day-book carries nine figures and a date and the names of nobody**, and the day-book stands at eleven entries and the register holds ten questions with no finding under any of them.
- **The practice does not run on the market mornings**, because the room over the weigh-house is open on them.
